articles.title: Amazon’s AI shopping assistant can now edit your grocery lists and gift registries
articles.summary: Amazon is updating its Alexa for Shopping assistant with several new features, including the ability to manage grocery lists and gift registries, as well as answer billing questions.
articles.body: Amazon is adding several new features to its AI shopping assistant, including ways to create, edit, and move items between shopping lists and gift registries. As an example, Amazon says you can now ask Alexa for Shopping to “Create a new shopping list” or “Show me what’s left on my wedding registry.” The ecommerce giant has continued to expand on its Alexa for Shopping assistant since its official launch in May, while resisting third-party AI shopping agents from companies like Meta and Perplexity. Alexa for Shopping lives next to the search bar across Amazon’s app and website, and can do things like set price alerts, compare items, and automatically purchase products when they drop below a set price. Along with the ability to manage registries and lists, Alexa for Shopping can now update your delivery instructions, answer billing questions about unrecognized charges and refunds, as well as pause and change recurring deliveries. These features are rolling out to customers in the US.

articles.title: Windows 11 can perform a full system reinstall via the cloud.
articles.summary:
The KB5127936 update includes a cloud rebuild feature that restores the OS and your device drivers from Windows Update when your PC is unable to boot. It requires an internet connection, but spares you from needing to keep a recovery USB drive handy, and doesn’t relying on the integrity of the current installation.

articles.title: In 1964, Georgian-style house was built in Charlotte, North Carolina; Decades later, Brooklyn Decker and Andy Roddick transformed the 7,000-square-foot fixer-upper into a colourful family home blending historic charm with personal design touches
articles.summary: Brooklyn Decker has opened the doors to the North Carolina house she and her husband, former tennis champion Andy Roddick, have spent years turning into a
articles.body: Brooklyn Decker has opened the doors to the North Carolina house she and her husband, former tennis champion Andy Roddick, have spent years turning into a true family home. The 7,000-square-foot Georgian-style house in Charlotte dates to 1964 and arrived in their lives as a genuine fixer-upper. One room had already caved in and water poured through the ceiling when they first saw it. Most of the house had barely been touched since it was built. Still, Decker, who grew up in the state, saw something worth saving: a solid neighbourhood, good bones, and the chance to put down roots after years of moving. What followed was a full gut renovation that kept the home’s traditional character while filling it with the colour and energy of family life.Brooklyn Decker’s house that needed everythingWhen the couple first walked through the property, they knew the work would be serious. Beyond the collapsed ceiling and water damage, the interiors felt frozen in time. Decker and Roddick became only the second owners. They had renovated homes before, but nothing on this scale. “We’d moved so many times [before this house],” Decker told Architectural Digest. “And we were excited to try something new. For us, that meant a historic house with some old Southern bones.” They brought in Ruard Veltman Architecture to rethink the structure and Stanwick Dunham for the contracting. The goal was to respect the original Georgian lines while making the house work for everyday family life.Brooklyn Decker’s design that stayed personalDecker took charge of the interiors herself. Over the past six years she has turned her love of decorating into professional work, including as a design partner with the firm By Idiots. She wanted to keep the house’s early character; what she described as “old English meets early Georgian meets Shaker”, while introducing modern comfort. Wallpaper with natural scenes, vintage patterned rugs, and a soft palette of muted greens, reds, blues, and yellows began to appear. The result was layered rather and a mix of history and the present.Colour led by Brooklyn Decker’s kidsThe biggest shift in the design came from listening to their children. Decker’s son Hank, now 10, and Stevie, 8, were given real say in the rooms around them. “When our kids became older, we really wanted to incorporate and take seriously what they wanted,” Decker explained. “Because, how cool to be eight and actually have some say in the space around you? So now the house is a hodgepodge of explosive colour, a lot of which is totally inspired and dictated by them.” The once-formal spaces now carry bright, playful energy that still sits comfortably inside the traditional architecture.A home that feels lived inThe finished house balances elegance with the mess and joy of family life. Original features remain visible, yet every room feels ready for daily use. Decker has described the process as both challenging and rewarding, a project that finally let the family settle into a place with history and heart. For a couple that had moved often, the Charlotte house represents a decision to stay put and build something lasting, one colourful room at a time.More on Brooklyn DeckerBrooklyn Decker is an American model, actress, and interior designer who rose to fame as a Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover star before transitioning into film and television roles. She has appeared in movies like ‘Just Go with It’ and the series ‘Grace and Frankie’. Married to former tennis champion Andy Roddick, she shares two children with him and has increasingly focused on design work. A Southern girl at heart, she is known for her down-to-earth style and lends a warm, personal element to her professional projects and family life.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Saath Nibhana Saathiya fame Devoleena Bhattacharjee defends women’s choice of keeping Karwa Chauth
articles.summary: Television actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee, who became a household name after playing the role of Gopi Bahu in Saath Nibhana Saathiya, celebrates all the
articles.body: Television actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee, who became a household name after playing the role of Gopi Bahu in Saath Nibhana Saathiya, celebrates all the festivals with the same excitement. Recently, the actress shared her opinion on Karwa Chauth, and the people celebrating the occasion.Devoleena, who is known for expressing her opinions freely and is quite vocal about her thoughts, took to her X account to speak about the festival of Karwa Chauth.On Thursday, the actress took to her X, formerly Twitter, and shared a long note in which she shared her perspective on the festival.She wrote, “Happy Karwa Chauth to all the beautiful ladies celebrating today. I’ve never kept a Karwa Chauth fast because, in Bengali and Assamese cultures, it isn’t a tradition. We may not have every ritual, but we celebrate so many festivals with all our hearts. So why not Karwa Chauth? Honestly, I do feel like keeping it someday. But I’m scared I won’t be able to manage a whole day without water. I fast every Monday and sometimes on Ekadashi, but water fasting? That’s a different story! But that’s not even the point. I genuinely feel that for many couples, this is a love language. I’ve seen women celebrate it happily, and today, so many husbands fast alongside their wives. So why bring feminism, patriarchy and judgment into someone else’s celebration? You don’t believe in it? Don’t celebrate it”.She went on to add that nobody is judging them but it’s not right to spoil someone else’s happiness.She further shared, “Mothers fast for their children, for their families. So if someone wishes to fast for her husband one day, why should that be a problem? As long as it’s a personal choice and nobody is forced into it, let people celebrate love the way they want to. And a little personal note, Shaan comes from a Muslim family, yet every Karwa Chauth, he asks me, ‘Tum rakhogi kya fast?’. And every year, I say, with a heavy heart, ‘Dekhte hain, next year’. I’m still breastfeeding, so hopefully next year! Because honestly, husbands deserve to feel special and loved too, don’t they? We do intermittent fasting, try keto and follow all kinds of diets for ourselves”.She concluded the note saying, "But when it comes to fasting for a husband, suddenly everything becomes about patriarchy and feminism? Ladies, thoda chill karo! Love is personal. Traditions are personal. Celebrations are personal. Let people choose what makes them happy. Happy Karwa Chauth to everyone celebrating! May your love always grow stronger."Devoleena got married to Shanawaz Shaikh on 14th of December 2022 in a private ceremony. Only close friends and family attended the wedding ceremony. The couple welcomed their first child, a baby boy named Joy in December 2024.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
articles.summary: Rivian reports $2.15B in Q3 revenue as the R2 becomes its best-selling EV, supported by surging software revenue and licensing deals with Volkswagen.
articles.body: Rivian reported its third quarter earnings of 2026, providing us a closer look at the company’s financial health as it ramps up production of its all-important R2 electric vehicle — which is now, for the first time, outselling all of Rivian’s other EVs. Rivian said it brought in $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase compared to the $1.558 billion in Q3 2025. Of that amount, $1.55 billion came from automotive revenue, which is up 36 percent year over year. Comparatively, the company reported $605 million from software and subscription services, a 45 percent increase year over year. As EV sales slow down, the company is seeking to make more money from its digital products, including the Autonomy Plus package. Automotive gross profits were on an upward trajectory, a sign that the company’s finances were improving as it delivered more vehicles. Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year. The company still lost $80 million in Q3 automotive gross profits, which is much better than the $130 million loss a year ago. In other words, Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle. (Also, the company continued to sell pollution credits to other carmakers, and also received a tariff refund from the government — all of which was recorded as revenue.) Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin. Most of this cash came from licensing their tech to Volkswagen, alongside customer subscriptions for Rivian’s Autonomy Plus driving features. In many ways, Rivian’s tech partnership with Volkswagen and software sales are currently paying the bills, keeping the company profitable overall while it absorbs a lot of heavy upfront costs from launching the R2. Earlier this month, Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. That represents an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries. (For a direct-to-consumer automaker like Rivian, deliveries serve as a proxy for sales.) Rivian doesn’t break down sales by model, so we don’t exactly how many R2s have reached customers so far. But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV). “We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon. “Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional.” The R2 was designed from the ground up to be Rivian’s higher-volume, mass-market offering — and by overtaking the company’s more expensive, lower-volume legacy vehicles, it seems to be doing just that. Still, the R2 isn’t bringing in the bulk of the revenue yet, as indicated by Rivian’s use of the phrase “by volume.” Most of the money is still coming from the VW partnership and its software division. But that could change once Rivian starts shipping the more affordable versions of the R2, like the $55,485 Premium trim (coming in late 2026), the $49,985 Standard Long-Range (early 2027), and the $46,495 Standard (late 2027). Developing…

articles.title: Reddit will force everyone to log in
articles.summary: Reddit is becoming a ‘logged-in-only experience,’ says CEO Steve Huffman.
articles.body: Reddit is announcing a huge shift: It’s going to start requiring users to log in. Right now, you can browse Reddit without having an account, and the site is generally a great resource for crowdsourced information on a whole range of topics. I know I’m not the only person who appends “reddit” to a lot of Google searches to find answers to things written by actual humans instead of robots. But that openness has made it a target for scraping and automated traffic, leading Reddit to file lawsuits over alleged unauthorized access of its data and make product changes like limiting access to “Old Reddit.” There’s no definitive timeline on when this change will roll out to all users, or how the site will work if you’re logged out. (If I send my friend a link to a thread and they aren’t logged in, what will they see?) To start, Reddit will test the logged-in requirement in “select markets outside the US” in the “coming months,” according to CEO Steve Huffman. “We’ll look at the impact on the user experience, on our business, and on the whole Reddit ecosystem, figure out where the right boundaries are, and go from there.” Reddit has also rebuilt and is rereleasing the Reddit app’s incognito mode. Huffman claims the login requirement is better for Reddit’s user experience and its ads business and is “more protective of Reddit data.” The “vast majority” of unauthorized Reddit access happens “through our logged-out experiences,” though the company will still strike licensing deals of its data with companies, like the deals it made with OpenAI and Google in 2024. Huffman notes that Reddit does not need to know a logged-in user’s identity — “Honestly, we don’t want to know” — just that the user is logged in at all. And he says that more logged-in users lets the company deliver “more relevant ads.” “This is a big change for Reddit, where we’ve allowed logged-out access to basically all of Reddit for the last two decades,” Huffman says. “And I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me. But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business.” Reddit is making this announcement alongside its Q3 2026 earnings, which were released today. Search traffic was “down meaningfully” in Q3, Huffman says in the company’s shareholder letter, with logged-out traffic and web traffic being the most heavily impacted. “During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” Huffman says. However, Huffman notes that app and logged-in daily active unique users make up “over 80% of the monetization on Reddit,” which he says “speaks to the strength of Reddit as a destination and the impact of our ongoing product work.”

articles.title: Reddit’s CEO says Google’s AI Mode ‘does not drive traffic’
articles.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said in an earnings call today that Google’s AI-powered search modes do not help with traffic to the platform.
articles.body: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said in an earnings call today that Google’s AI-powered search modes do not help with traffic to the platform, echoing problems facing other websites and publishers. As part of its Q3 2026 earnings, Reddit revealed that search traffic in October has “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” and he attributes part of the company’s struggles with Google traffic to how AI Mode and AI Overviews change the search experience. “The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic,” Huffman says. “Not for us, and not to anybody, as far as I know. That’s just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it’s not.” He says that AI Overviews and AI Mode have “evolved a lot” and now, at a “minimum,” push “everyone down the search page.” Huffman also says that Reddit believes its content that’s machine-translated into other languages is being ranked lower in search results, which he says would primarily affect the company outside the US. However, Reddit is still a “top search term in Google,” Huffman says. “This doesn’t say anything about the internet consumers’ demand for Reddit. People still want Reddit. It says Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to.” He also says that Google is “crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn’t changed from their point of view, either.” (Google’s business has been affected by AI Mode, too: it said yesterday that it’s seeing “lower monetization” in AI Mode ads, though it’s now bringing AI ads to more countries.) To try and combat the search referral difficulties, Reddit is working to make the platform a “direct, sticky, daily destination.” Yesterday, it introduced a “For You” feed with recommendations related to your interests, and in August, it started testing an experiment that uses AI to turn posts into short videos. Reddit also announced today that it’s going to force everyone to log in, which Huffman claims will be “better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data.”
